note: The electrolyte model (GAME_SPEC §10): Pitzer's equations at 25 C, used at every temperature. a_phi and b: the Debye-Huckel term. pairs: a cation and an anion, named as in species.json's ions, with beta0, beta1, beta2, c_phi and the exponents alpha1, alpha2. A pair not listed has no specific interaction. diffusion: each ion's diffusion coefficient at 25 C, scaled to other temperatures as T / viscosity (GAME_SPEC §7); an ion not listed puts no limit on transport. viscosity: the solvent's (water's, at 0.5 MPa: the liquid to 150 C), mPa s, by rising temperature; read between points in its logarithm, held beyond the ends. solvent: saturated liquid water's properties by temperature (Lienhard, A Heat Transfer Textbook 6.00, Table A.3: rho kg/m3, cp J/kg K, k W/m K, alpha and nu m2/s, Pr, beta 1/K), read between rows, held beyond the ends: its density, for what floats on what (a column's layers, GAME_SPEC §6), its conduction, and boiling's bubbles (§11). water_ionisation: water's own ionisation, whose constant Kw sets the pH where neither an acid nor a base is left over. Sources: docs/DATA_SOURCES.md.

diffusion.note: each ion's diffusion coefficient in water at infinite dilution, 25 C, m2/s (GAME_SPEC §7)

density.note: the solvent's density at 1 atm (Stage 67: what a liquid's and a solute's volume grow by with temperature), kg/m^3: (a0 + a1 t + ... + a5 t^5) / (1 + b t), t in C, its range in C; beyond it, its value and slope at the end
